question: Your extraction pipeline validates each output with Pydantic and retries failed extractions, appending the specific validation errors to the prompt. A review of the failures shows two groups. Some invoices return dates as "03/14/2024" when the schema requires ISO 8601 format. Other invoices fail because the payment terms field is empty, and those invoices state only "terms per master agreement," a document that is never given to the system. Which conclusions about the retry loop are correct?

options.text: Both groups of failures should bypass the retry loop and go straight to human review, because retries cannot correct any kind of validation failure.
options.reason: The guide distinguishes the cases: retry with error feedback works for format and structural errors, so it remains useful for the date failures.

options.text: Raising the retry limit for the payment terms failures will eventually produce valid terms, because each attempt gives the model another chance to find them.
options.reason: No number of retries can produce information that is absent from the source document, so more attempts only waste calls or invite fabricated values.

options.text: Retrying the date failures with the specific format error appended is likely to succeed, because the model can correct a format mismatch.
options.reason: The guide says that retries succeed for format mismatches and structural output errors, especially when the specific validation error is fed back.

options.text: Retrying the payment terms failures will not help, because the terms exist only in the master agreement, which the extraction system never receives.
options.reason: The guide says that retries are ineffective when the required information is absent from the source, for example when it exists only in an external document that was not provided.

options.text: The date failures will persist under retry, because the dates come from the source document and the model cannot change how the source writes them.
options.reason: The date value is present in the source, and only its output format is wrong. The guide treats such format mismatches as errors that retries can fix.
